title: How did towns of the Swahili coast trade across the ocean?
answer: For centuries, merchants from towns along the eastern coast of Africa traded across the Indian Ocean. Sailors learned when winds were likely to carry boats toward Africa or away from it. Coastal traders sent some goods inland and received others, such as gold, from networks farther into Africa. Ships also brought goods such as pottery made across the ocean. Finds in coastal houses give clues about these trips. They show that the towns were part of a much wider trade network.
facts: Many trading towns along the coast were connected by the use of the Swahili language.

title: What do old buildings on an island in Tanzania reveal about trade?
answer: Kilwa Kisiwani was a Swahili town on an island just off what is now Tanzania. Its people built homes, places of worship, and a palace using stone, including rock formed by coral. Among the ruins, archaeologists found pieces of pottery that had traveled from places far across the Indian Ocean. The pottery helps trace trade routes that no longer have the same stopovers. Looking at both the buildings and the small objects gives clues about how Kilwa became a busy and wealthy port.
facts: The ruins of another nearby Swahili town are on Songo Mnara.

title: Where did Zheng He’s fleets travel?
answer: In the early 1400s, the rulers of Ming China sent fleets of ships across the Indian Ocean. A leader named Zheng He commanded several of these journeys. The ships stopped in ports in Southeast Asia, along India, and as far away as eastern Africa. Members of the fleets met rulers and carried gifts and goods. Rather than sailing into an empty sea, they traveled along routes where many groups already traded. The journeys show how far people and goods could move by ship.
facts: Zheng He is usually credited with leading seven voyages between 1405 and 1433.

title: Why did more people begin working in factories?
answer: For a long time, people could spin thread or weave cloth in homes and small workshops. In Britain, larger machines made it possible to gather several parts of this work in one place. Water or steam could power machines in a mill, and many workers could work under the same roof. Cloth could be made more quickly, but workers had to keep to the machines’ pace and often worked long days. Changes like these also helped industrial cities grow.
facts: Cotton mills helped Manchester grow into a large industrial city.

title: How did Haiti become an independent country?
answer: France once ruled a colony in the western part of the island of Hispaniola, where many people were enslaved on plantations. In 1791, enslaved people began a large uprising. Fighting lasted for years and included groups with different goals. Toussaint Louverture helped lead forces that had fought to end slavery. After further conflict, Haitian leaders declared independence in 1804. The new country’s beginning showed that people who had lived through slavery could win freedom and build a state of their own.
facts: Toussaint Louverture died before Haiti declared independence.

title: What changed for Japan during the Meiji Restoration?
answer: In 1868, Japan’s government changed after centuries during which military rulers called shoguns had held much of its power. A new government ruled in the name of the emperor, whose reign was called Meiji. Leaders changed the way regions were governed and studied ways of building schools, railways, and industry. People in different walks of life had to learn how to work with new rules and opportunities. Change was uneven, and many older ways of living continued alongside new ones.
facts: The city formerly called Edo became known as Tokyo near the start of the Meiji period.

title: Why did people dig a canal across part of Egypt?
answer: The Suez Canal links the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea through Egypt. A ship traveling between parts of Europe and Asia can use it rather than going all the way around southern Africa. Workers had to cut a long channel across fairly low desert land and through some lakes. The canal opened to shipping in 1869. Many ships that once made the longer trip around Africa could then follow a shorter route through Egypt.
facts: The Suez Canal has no locks because ships move along a channel at sea level.

title: How did the Panama Canal change ocean travel?
answer: Before the Panama Canal opened, ships traveling between the Atlantic and Pacific sides of the Americas often had to sail far around South America. Workers in Panama dug through hills, built dams, and made locks to raise ships to a lake and lower them again. The canal opened to traffic in 1914. The United States managed it for decades before agreements set a date for Panama to take over. Panama began managing the whole canal at the end of 1999.

facts: The official opening was marked by a passage of the ship Ancon in August 1914.

title: What happened on November 11, 1918?
answer: By late 1918, the First World War had gone on for more than four years. Representatives of Germany and the countries fighting it agreed to an armistice, a promise to stop fighting under specific terms. It took effect at eleven in the morning on November 11 on the Western Front. The agreement came before the final peace treaties. Many places still observe the date today to remember people affected by the war and later wars.
facts: The agreement was signed in a railway carriage in France.

title: Why did countries create the League of Nations?
answer: After the First World War, leaders wanted countries to have a place to talk through disagreements before turning to fighting. The League of Nations began in 1920, with its center in Geneva, Switzerland. Countries sent representatives to meetings and tried to cooperate on difficult problems. Some important countries did not join or left over time. The League could not stop the Second World War. Its work and problems helped leaders think about how to build another organization after that war.

facts: The United States never joined the League, even though a US president had helped propose it.

title: Why did countries form the United Nations?
answer: Near the end of the Second World War, delegates from many countries came to San Francisco. They wrote a charter for an organization called the United Nations. They wanted countries to talk about conflicts, work together on problems, and support equal rights. Member countries can still disagree, so meetings and rules do not make every problem easy to solve. The United Nations gives countries a shared place to discuss some problems affecting more than one country.
facts: The United Nations Charter went into effect on October 24, 1945.

title: What does the Universal Declaration of Human Rights say?
answer: In 1948, representatives at the United Nations agreed on a statement about basic rights that people everywhere should have. It describes freedoms and protections that belong to people because they are human. The statement includes ideas about safety, fair treatment, education, and the ability to share beliefs. It sets out goals and principles rather than a set of rules enforced by one world government. Later laws and treaties have drawn on it in different ways.
facts: The declaration says that all people are born free and equal in dignity and rights.

title: Why was Berlin once divided by a wall?
answer: After the Second World War, Germany and the city of Berlin were split into areas controlled by different governments. In 1961, East German leaders built a barrier through and around West Berlin to stop people from leaving across the city’s border. The wall split streets and made it hard for neighbors and families to visit. In 1989 crowds gathered at border crossings after officials announced a change, and guards began letting people through. Germany reunited the following year.
facts: The border crossings opened on the night of November 9, 1989.

title: What was apartheid in South Africa?
answer: Apartheid was a system of laws in South Africa that separated people by race. It gave white people most political power and put limits on where many other people could live, travel, study, or work. South Africans opposed the system in many ways, and people in other countries added pressure. Over time, leaders agreed to end the laws and hold an election open to adult citizens of all races. That election in 1994 marked a big change.

facts: Laws enforcing apartheid were strengthened after the National Party came to power in 1948.

title: How did Nelson Mandela help change South Africa?
answer: Nelson Mandela helped organize against apartheid, the system that denied many people equal rights in South Africa. He spent many years in prison. After his release, he took part in talks about ending apartheid and preparing a new election. In 1994, South Africa held its first fully democratic national election. Citizens of all races could vote, and Mandela became president. Many people did this work alongside him, and changing the law did not quickly solve every problem they faced.
